title: BA1/1889/2023 of GAGAN Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Bail Application No.1889 of 2023
Gagan ........Applicant

Present:-
Mr. Avidit Noliyal, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Bhaskar Chandra Joshi, AGA for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The applicant is in judicial custody FIR/Case
Crime No.242 of 2023, dated 15.03.2023, under Sections
394, 397, 457, 411, 34 IPC and Sections 3/25 of the
Arms Act, 1959, Police Station Kotwali Laksar, District
Haridwar. He has sought his release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. According to the FIR, on 15.03.2023, the
informant was sleeping in his courtyard. At about 03:15
AM, early in the morning, three miscreants entered into
his house, who had lathi-danda, country-made pistol
and torch. They started searching in the house. In the
meanwhile, the informant and his son, both noticed the
activities and objected to the act of the miscreants, but

2
they attacked on the informant and his family members
and also opened fired. In the scuffle, one of the
miscreants was arrested, who is the applicant.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that the applicant did not commit any offence;
he was a Labourer or Coolie; they were returning home
while talking loudly; while they were moving from near
the house of the informant, some dispute took place
between the applicant and the informant. That dispute
took the shape of a quarrel, in which, two associates of
the applicant managed to escape and the applicant was
apprehended by the informant.
5. Learned State counsel would submit that the
applicant and his associates attacked on the informant
and his family members. They entered into the house at
an early hours of the day when the applicant caught red
handed.
6. The applicant was apprehended at about
03:00 - 03:15 AM early in the morning when he entered
with the intention of loot, etc. They caused injuries. It is
a very serious offence. There is no ground to enlarge the
applicant on bail.

3
7. Having considered, this Court is of the view
that it is not a case fit for bail and the bail application
of the applicant deserves to be rejected.
8. The bail application is rejected.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 02.05.2024
Sanjay
